data.description:
# Smarter AI hand acquisition: gate expensive businesses and untargeted upgrades

## Problem statement

The Main Street AI decides which market cards to take into its hand using a
single proxy — the card's listed cost — so it hoards cards it cannot pay for
and cards it can never use. It moves a very expensive business into a hand
slot even when it owns no income-producing business (so it has no route to
ever affording it), and it moves an upgrade card into the hand even when it
does not own the upgrade's target business. Both behaviours clog the
three-slot hand and waste the week's action, making the AI measurably weaker
and less believable than a human playing the same position.

## Users

- **Main Street player (human vs AI / competitive mode)** — wants an AI
  opponent whose market and hand decisions look deliberate, so the opponent
  is a credible challenge rather than a card-hoarder.
- **Game designer / balance engineer** — wants AI heuristics that do not
  distort Monte Carlo balance data with obviously wasted actions.
- **Developer** — wants the acquisition heuristic documented and unit-tested
  so future behaviour changes are traceable.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want the AI to stop parking an unaffordable
  business in its hand when it has no income, so that its hand holds cards it
  can actually use.
- As a competitive player, I want the AI to hold an upgrade only for a
  business it actually owns, so that its upgrades are meaningful.
- As a balance engineer, I want the acquisition gates covered by unit tests
  and documented, so that AI-behaviour regressions are visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Expensive-business gate.** In the heuristic AI (`GreedyStrategy`,
   `BankingGreedyStrategy`, and the competitive `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`),
   a `move-to-hand` action for a card of family `business` is **not selected**
   when both (a) the card's effective play cost exceeds the acting seat's
   current coins and (b) the acting seat has no income stream — i.e. none of
   its placed businesses has `baseIncome > 0`. When the seat does have an
   income stream, or when the card is affordable, the existing
   acquisition behaviour is unchanged.
2. **Untargeted-upgrade gate.** A `move-to-hand` action for a card of family
   `upgrade` is **not selected** unless the acting seat owns the upgrade's
   `targetBusiness` at the required level (`name === targetBusiness`,
   `level === requiredLevel`, `level < maxLevel`), matching the existing
   apply/play eligibility. Upgrades whose target is owned remain eligible.
3. **Parity across strategies.** The two gates are applied consistently in
   single-player and competitive heuristic strategies (the codebase already
   mirrors the single-player acquisition scorer in the competitive scorer);
   `RandomStrategy` remains an unchanged random baseline and is documented as
   such.
4. **No regression for legitimate acquisition.** Cards that pass both gates
   are still taken to hand exactly as before: an affordable business, an
   unaffordable business when an income stream exists, and an upgrade whose
   target is owned at the required level. The existing greedy-vs-banking
   behavioural distinction remains demonstrable (the `ai-banking-strategy`
   scenario is updated if the old scenario can no longer distinguish them).
5. **Tests.** Unit tests cover the four gate combinations for both gates
   (business: affordable/unaffordable × income/no-income; upgrade:
   target-owned/target-absent, plus wrong-level), and assert that the
   heuristic strategies never emit the gated `move-to-hand` actions. At least
   one test exercises the decision through `chooseAction` (not only the pure
   scorer).
6. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` documents both gates,
   defines "income stream", "affordable" and "owns the target business", and
   states which strategies the gates apply to. All related documentation and
   code comments are updated to reflect the changes, including the README and
   any relevant docs-site entries (only where they reference the acquisition
   heuristic).
7. **Balance guardrail.** The Monte Carlo guardrail suite
   (`tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`) passes for `greedy` and
   `banking-greedy`; if it shifts, a drift report is produced and recorded on
   this work item as evidence.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Heuristic only; no new engine mechanic.** The change is confined to AI
  acquisition scoring/selection in `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` plus
  documentation and tests. No CSV, engine, state or save-format change is
  expected.
- **Reuse existing helpers.** Effective business cost uses
  `computeEffectiveBusinessPurchaseCost`; upgrade target eligibility mirrors
  `canPurchaseUpgrade` / the play-upgrade-from-hand enumeration
  (`biz.name === targetBusiness`, `biz.level === requiredLevel`,
  `biz.level < biz.maxLevel`) and the competitive `competitiveUpgradeTargets`.
- **Do not remove `move-to-hand` from enumeration** unless required: prefer
  scoring/gating so `RandomStrategy` stays a true random baseline and the
  change is additive. If the chosen implementation filters enumeration, the
  documented baseline behaviour must be updated explicitly.
- **Determinism.** No new RNG; same seed + state ⇒ same decision.
- **Scope discipline.** The seed is about *taking cards into hand*. Do not
  change direct purchase paths (`buy-business`, `buy-upgrade`, `buy-event`) —
  `buy-upgrade` already requires an owned target at the required level.
- **Community spaces** are out of scope for the income-stream gate (the seed
  says "businesses"); they already carry their own placement gating. If the
  producer wants them covered, record it as a follow-up work item.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
  - `scoreMarketAcquisition(state, action)` (~L1120): for `move-to-hand` it
    returns the market card's listed `cost` as a "lock-in value" proxy; no
    affordability, income or target-ownership check.
  - `enumerateLegalActions` (~L836): enumerates `move-to-hand` for every
    non-staff, non-event market card whenever `canAddToHand` is legal,
    regardless of cost or upgrade target.
  - `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 5 (~L1317): takes the highest-scoring
    `move-to-hand` / `buy-event` action when its score is `> 0`. Since a
    `move-to-hand` score is the card's cost, any positive-cost card is taken.
  - Competitive mirror: `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` (~L2597) and the
    `move-to-hand` branch of `competitiveScore` (~L2237) both return the
    listed cost; `competitiveBestMarketAcquisitionValue` (~L2270) does the
    same for the discard-capacity benefit.
  - `bestVisibleBankTarget` / `bestPipelineBankTarget` (~L437–L535) already
    value *unaffordable* cards as banking targets — related but out of scope
    (the seed is about the hand, not about banking actions).
- `src/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `canAddToHand`, `canPurchaseUpgrade`,
  `effectiveUpgradeCost`, `bestEffectiveUpgradeCost` provide the eligibility
  primitives.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeEffectiveBusinessPurchaseCost`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId` for competitive ownership.
- Tests today: `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` (enumeration/scoring),
  `ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (L124–L136 asserts `GreedyStrategy` returns
  `move-to-hand` for an unaffordable Mega Mall — an existing scenario that
  this change will affect), `competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts`,
  `ai-upgrade-budget.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` documents the market-acquisition
  tier ("the card's listed cost — a proxy for how valuable it is to lock in
  ahead of payment") and the mirrored competitive scorer.

## Desired change

- Add two acquisition gates to the heuristic `move-to-hand` decision:
  1. **Business**: skip an unaffordable business when the seat has no
     income-producing business on the street.
  2. **Upgrade**: skip an upgrade unless the seat owns its `targetBusiness`
     at the required level.
- Apply the gates in both the single-player acquisition scorer
  (`scoreMarketAcquisition` / `bestMarketAcquisitionValue`) and the
  competitive mirror (`competitiveScore` `move-to-hand` branch /
  `competitiveBestMarketAcquisitionValue`), so saturated/discard and banking
  logic stays consistent with what can actually be taken to hand.
- Introduce small, named predicate helpers (e.g. `hasIncomeStream(state,
  playerId?)` and `ownsUpgradeTarget(state, card, playerId?)`) so the rule is
  expressed once and reused, with doc comments referencing this work item.
- Keep `RandomStrategy` unchanged; document the acquisition gates in
  `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Add failing unit tests for the four gate combinations (business × income,
   upgrade × owned target) through the pure scorer and through `chooseAction`.
2. Update the `ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` greedy-vs-banking scenario so the
   two strategies remain distinguishable under the new gate.
3. Implement the predicates and gate the single-player and competitive
   acquisition scoring.
4. Update `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` and any code comments.
5. Run the Monte Carlo guardrail suite (AC7) and the full suite (AC8).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — add `hasIncomeStream` / `ownsUpgradeTarget`
  predicates; gate `scoreMarketAcquisition`, `bestMarketAcquisitionValue`,
  the competitive `move-to-hand` score and
  `competitiveBestMarketAcquisitionValue`; update doc comments.
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` — new gate tests (business × income,
  upgrade × owned target, wrong level).
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` — update the greedy-vs-banking
  scenario (L124–L136) so it still distinguishes the two strategies.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — competitive mirror
  gate tests.
- `tests/main-street/ai-upgrade-budget.test.ts` — verify upgrade
  enumeration/budget tests still hold and extend if needed.
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the two acquisition gates and
  their definitions.
- `src/MainStreetMarket.ts` — likely no change (reuse `canAddToHand`,
  `bestEffectiveUpgradeCost`); verify.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — likely no change (reuse
  `computeEffectiveBusinessPurchaseCost`); verify.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW` — AI uses community space cards too much (done) —
  same class of fix: a smarter hand/placement heuristic with tests + docs.
- `MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y` — AI should not use Community Favour as much (done) —
  heuristic gating with documented thresholds and evidence.
- `MS-0MUYODDW300690KX` — AI should not place synergies that only benefit the
  player (done) — AI decision-quality fix in the same module.
- `MS-0MUX6PMCE002I6HO` — Ai should check win conditions (done) — adjacent
  AI-decision correctness work.
- `MS-0MT5X3N79002S038` — Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free
  scoring for shared-street play (done) — the competitive scorer's origin.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — Some staff cards should add action points (done) —
  context on hand-slot capacity as a build axis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (income stream).** "Income stream" = the acting seat has at
  least one placed business with `baseIncome > 0` (not present income in
  `resourceBank.coins`, which is a stock, not a stream). *If the producer
  prefers a stricter definition (e.g. positive projected income after
  running costs), adjust AC1.*
- **Assumption (expensive).** "Very expensive" is operationalised as
  *unaffordable* (effective cost > current coins), not an absolute threshold,
  combined with the no-income condition. This keeps the rule proportional to
  the seat's economy. *If an absolute threshold is wanted, it can be layered on
  top.*
- **Assumption (owns target).** The upgrade target must be owned at the
  *required* level (matching apply eligibility), not merely present at any
  level.
- **Test-churn risk.** The existing `ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` greedy-vs-
  banking scenario relies on the current "always move-to-hand" behaviour and
  will need a new distinguishing state. Mitigation: AC4 requires the greedy
  vs banking distinction to remain demonstrable.
- **Balance risk.** Reducing hand clogging should improve AI strength, which
  may shift Monte Carlo metrics. Mitigation: AC7 runs the guardrail suite and
  records any drift; snapshot regeneration follows the repo's drift policy
  (`scripts/balance/drift-report.ts`) and requires producer approval.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Adjacent asks (banking-target selection for
  no-income seats, community-space acquisition gating, direct-purchase paths)
  are out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items, not
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-10-12):** "How is 'very expensive'
  defined — (a) unaffordable relative to current coins, (b) an absolute coin
  threshold, or (c) unaffordable AND above a threshold?" — Answer: **not
  received (non-interactive dispatch)**; proceeded with default **(a)
  unaffordable relative to current coins**, combined with the no-income
  condition, as the most proportional and testable reading of the seed.
- **Q2 (same dispatch):** "What counts as 'an income stream' — (a) owns at
  least one placed business with `baseIncome > 0`, or (b) positive projected
  net income after running costs?" — Answer: **not received**; proceeded with
  default **(a)** (simple, deterministic, observable on the street).
- **Q3 (same dispatch):** "For upgrades, does 'owns the appropriate
  business' mean the target at the required level, or merely present at any
  level?" — Answer: **not received**; proceeded with **required level**,
  matching the existing apply/play eligibility so the gate cannot diverge from
  what the AI could actually use.
- **Q4 (same dispatch):** "Should the gate apply to the competitive AI too?" —
  Answer: **not received**; proceeded with **yes** (AC3), because the
  single-player and competitive acquisition scorers are already mirrored and
  the seed says "the AI" without qualifying the mode.

### Research findings (agent, 2026-10-12)

- The acquisition proxy is exactly as described: `scoreMarketAcquisition`
  returns `card.cost` for `move-to-hand` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:1120`),
  and `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 5 takes it whenever the score is `> 0`
  (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:1317`). No affordability, income or target
  check exists on that path.
- Enumeration offers `move-to-hand` for every non-staff, non-event market
  card whenever `canAddToHand` is legal (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:836`),
  and the competitive enumeration mirrors this (`…:2112`).
- The existing `ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (L124–L136) explicitly asserts
  that `GreedyStrategy` chooses `move-to-hand` for a 5000-cost Mega Mall with
  only 1000 coins and no income — i.e. it codifies the behaviour this work
  item changes, so that test must be updated.
- Upgrade play/apply eligibility already requires the target at the required
  level (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:865–L872`), giving a ready-made
  predicate for the upgrade gate.

## Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG** – Documentation: Main Street card packs (DLC) cross-reference (completed)
- **MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X** – Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships, upgrade chains and community spaces (open)
